title: Micah: under the fig tree (Micah 4:4)
hookLine: each under their vine and fig tree, "and none shall make them afraid"

lines: DOWN TO ONE PATCH OF SHADE.
cards: A fig tree throws real shade. Its leaves are broad, and on a hot afternoon the ground under one is cool and green.
Micah's fourth chapter starts enormous: the mountain of the LORD's house raised above the hills, and peoples streaming toward it to learn.

Then the line about swords, in the King James: "they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks." Nation shall not lift up a sword against nation. That's the view from high up.
Then Micah comes all the way down, to one person in one patch of shade.

teach.h: SIT: NOBODY HAS TO WATCH THE ROAD.
teach.b: Here's the verse: "But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid." Every piece is doing work. Sit: not marching, not working, not standing guard.
Sitting is what you do when you don't have to watch the road.

teach.h: HIS OWN VINE, HIS OWN FIG TREE.
teach.b: His vine, his fig tree: his own, not rented, borrowed or taken. Someone who expects to stay.

teach.h: AND NONE SHALL MAKE THEM AFRAID.
teach.b: And the last phrase, short in Hebrew: ve'ein macharid, and none shall make them tremble. That's how Micah measures peace.

Not by a treaty, not by a map with no battles on it, but by whether a person sitting in their own yard has anything left to flinch at. The swords are gone, but the vision isn't finished until the fear is gone too.
The picture has a past. In the book of Kings, in Solomon's days, Judah and Israel are said to have lived safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree.
So Micah's hope reaches back to a remembered good time and promises it again, for everyone. The verse ends with a signature: for the mouth of the LORD of hosts hath spoken it.
And it comes close to home, because what makes people afraid is often small and near: a tone of voice, a door slammed, a person who might laugh at you. The vision is as big as the nations.

teach.h: THE LAST LINE FITS IN A KITCHEN.
teach.b: Its last line fits in a kitchen.

how: Jews read Micah among the Twelve, and the hope of each person under their own vine and fig tree is sung and quoted in Jewish life as a picture of peace without fear.

games.why: Micah comes down from nations to one person: "they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid."

practice: Notice anything in you that's braced, shoulders up, jaw tight, and let a little of it go, the way you would sitting in shade.

Then bring to mind one person who might be braced around you, a child, a coworker who answers to you, a careful friend, and ask what would let them sit easy in your company: a softer voice, a promise kept, telling them plainly they're not in trouble.
If you pray, you can say Micah's line for them.

wordCard.voice: Micah. The prophet who brought the peace of nations down to one person under a vine and a fig tree, with nothing to be afraid of. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: "and none makes them tremble," the last words of Micah's picture of peace.

carryVoice: Your line: none shall make them afraid. Peace, measured in one patch of shade. Until tomorrow.
